correctness.rationale: Squaring the specified average y/2 at either face and taking the centered flux divergence gives −y³/(2h²), so freezing the coefficient in backward Euler gives exactly F_T after division by b. The cubic z+Tz³−1 is strictly increasing and has one positive root s. Expanding F_T∘F_T verifies the factored displacement in RESULT.md; its denominator is positive and the quadratic changes root count at T=4. For T≤4 the displacement points toward s on both sides. For T>4 the two roots p_± satisfy p_++p_−=1 and Tp_+p_−=1 and are exchanged by F_T, hence straddle s. The displacement points toward p_− below s and p_+ above s; because F_T² is increasing, iterates are trapped between the start and the attracting fixed point of F_T² on that side. This clarifies the proof's shorthand 'bounded by fixed points': an outer bound can be the starting value, not another fixed point. Chain differentiation on the cycle gives 4/T. At T=4 the quadratic is 4v² for v=z−1/2, the cubic is 4v+O(v²), and the denominator is 8+O(v); thus v advances to v−2v³+O(v⁴) per two steps. The inverse-square increment tends to 4, so jv_(2j)²→1/4, and the odd-to-even deviation ratio tends to −1. The full-index limit is 1/2 for every nonfixed positive start, including the assigned start 1. The damped multiplier is 1−ω(3−2s), with s→0 as T→∞; precisely 0<ω≤2/3 gives strict local linear stability at every finite T. This proves no globally damped convergence assertion. The supplied verification files were inspected; the frozen code was not run.
